text:
Rishi Malhotra: heads up — gross margin model needs updated meter assumptions after the token + cache + retry fixes. I’m refreshing the Feb forecast + Q2 packaging scenarios and the deltas are big enough that I don’t want to “guess” defaults.

Rishi Malhotra: Specifically need guidance on:
1) billed_tokens vs raw_tokens semantics post changes
2) cache-hit attribution (what % of prompt tokens become non-billable / discounted, if any)
3) retries/fallback dedupe: expected reduction in “billed token inflation”
4) region dimension fix: how to split COGS by region going forward

Rishi Malhotra: Can someone from Eng/Product confirm what changes we should assume in the margin model for March onward? Also: do we need a pre/post segmentation for experiment readouts? (I think yes)

Laura Bennett: +1. Let’s be crisp here — we can’t have Finance modeling on a moving target. @Nadia Rahman @Mei Lin can you outline “before vs after” in plain English + any expected magnitude ranges from shadow billing?

Emily Stone: Also please call out anything that changes revrec source-of-truth tables or impacts invoice preview / close. Even if we aren’t retro-adjusting, we need to document the assumption change.

Nikhil Sharma: looping in @Chris Osei as well — experiments overlap w/ some of these fixes. We’ve already got a caveat note but need concrete “start using new meter fields as of X”.

Nadia Rahman: yup. quick summary here; I’ll follow w/ a longer note.

Nadia Rahman: What’s changing (Hosted API):
- We’re standardizing to `billed_tokens` for customer billing + internal revenue reporting.
- `raw_tokens` remains available for debugging / “what model emitted/consumed” but is not the billing basis.
- Streaming partials + server-side fallback/retry were double-counting in some paths. Fix is in progress / rolling out w/ shadow compare.
- Cache attribution fields are being populated more consistently (cache_hit / cached_prompt_tokens), which affects cost attribution + experiment analysis.

Nadia Rahman: Important: cache doesn’t necessarily mean “non-billable” — it’s mostly a COGS lever (less compute). Billing policy depends on the packaging rules (separate doc). For now, billed tokens are tokens we charge for per usage definition; cache-hit just annotates that some compute may have been saved.

Rishi Malhotra: super helpful. For margin model I need to translate that into unit economics inputs. Two asks:
A) expected delta between old “tokens” metric vs `billed_tokens` once retry double-counting is fixed
B) how much COGS reduction we attribute to cache hits (e.g., assume cached_prompt_tokens have ~0 incremental GPU cost?)

Mei Lin: I can pull shadow billing compare aggregates by account/model/region. From the week-1 run, the biggest delta was retry duplication. Roughly: 0.3–1.2% of requests showed duplicate usage_event_ids in some failure modes, but token impact clustered in a few high-volume streaming customers.

Mei Lin: I’ll share a quick table: “old meter billed_tokens_estimate vs new billed_tokens” by day for Feb 10–Feb 24. We should treat as directional until rollout hits 100%.

Caleb Johnson: re: cache fields — we’re backfilling missing `cache_hit` + `cached_prompt_tokens` for the last ~30 days for analysis only. Finance should not assume historic invoices will be regenerated.

Emily Stone: ^ please repeat that last line in whatever write-up we store for audit. “No retroactive invoice changes without approval.”

Nikhil Sharma: On packaging side: current pricing still charges on billed tokens (prompt+completion) even if prompt was served from cache. We do NOT have a “cache-discount” on invoices today.

Nikhil Sharma: BUT: for gross margin we should treat cached prompt tokens as lower cost because they avoid some prefill compute. So margin improves even if revenue doesn’t change.

Rishi Malhotra: great. can we quantify the cache COGS benefit? even a rough multiplier for “cached prompt token cost vs uncached prompt token cost”.

Nadia Rahman: We don’t have a single constant; depends on model + sequence length + batching. But for modeling you can approximate:
- uncached prompt tokens: full prefill cost
- cached prompt tokens: near-zero prefill cost (not literally zero, but materially lower)
- completion tokens: unchanged

Nadia Rahman: If you need a simplification: treat cached prompt tokens as 10–20% of uncached prompt token GPU cost. That’s consistent w/ perf runs on the common seq length buckets. (We can refine after perf-canary + more telemetry stabilizes.)

Laura Bennett: Rishi, use that range and show sensitivity bands. We can tighten later.

Chris Osei: on segmentation: yes, we should explicitly segment analyses pre/post meter fixes. For Q1 experiments, we should tag an “analysis validity window” and exclude the few days where shadow compare shows unstable deltas.

Chris Osei: Proposed cutoff for analyses: “new meter semantics stable starting Mar 1” (tentative) — but depends on rollout completion + backfill notes from @Mei Lin.

Mei Lin: rollout status (as of today):
- retry/fallback dedupe fix: 60% traffic (hosted) behind flag
- region dimension fix: already at ~95% (some legacy edge paths)
- embeddings batch fix: rolling out separately (affects embeddings meters only)

Mei Lin: I’d be comfortable calling “stable” once dedupe fix is >95% and drift dashboard shows <0.25% delta vs ledger for 7 consecutive days.

Rishi Malhotra: ok, I’ll do:
- Feb actuals: leave as-is, document known meter inflation risk
- March+ forecast: assume billed_tokens decrease by 0.5% baseline (with 0–1.5% sensitivity) due to dedupe
- COGS: apply cache multiplier (cached prompt token cost = 15% of uncached) and use observed cache-hit rate from new fields once stable
- Region: split COGS by region using corrected dimension; pre-fix months keep old allocation

Rishi Malhotra: sanity check: does `billed_tokens` include tool call tokens? (some customers asking)

Nadia Rahman: yes, tool/function calling tokens are included in billed_tokens under the same tokenization rules; they’re attributed to the parent request_id. New unit tests cover this.

Emily Stone: and for revrec: we continue to use billing ledger as the basis; usage events are supporting. If the ledger-to-usage drift breaches threshold, we treat it as an incident and document the month-end exception handling.

Laura Bennett: action items:
- @Mei Lin send Rishi the shadow compare delta table + recommended “stable start date” when we hit thresholds
- @Nadia Rahman drop a short write-up (bullet points) we can paste into the margin model assumptions tab + close memo
- @Rishi Malhotra share updated GM model with sensitivity bands + call out the pre/post meter segmentation for experiments

Rishi Malhotra: will do. I’ll post the updated sheet link in this thread once numbers are in.

Mei Lin: sharing here (internal link): snowflake export `finance.recon_usage_daily_v1` has both `billed_tokens_old` and `billed_tokens_new` during shadow mode. Use `meter_version` filter. Ping me if access blocked (it’s gated).

Rishi Malhotra: perfect, thanks. requesting access now if needed.

Emily Stone: please route through INT ticket for access (audit logging). :thumbsup:

Rishi Malhotra: ack.

Nikhil Sharma: one more note: for any experiment readout charts, we should label “meter_v1/v2 boundary” on the timeline so nobody misreads conversion/ARPU shifts.

Chris Osei: +1, I’ll add a standard annotation in the readout template.
